answer: Sybil resistance can rest on audit sampling. Each submitted task is hashed into a verifiable random draw that picks three reviewers from the validator pool, and each stakes before voting. To fake work, an attacker must control all three reviewers for that task, so the odds fall as the cube of its pool share, and the capital at risk grows faster than any payout. A ring that attests its own duplicates earns nothing extra, and one honest audit slashes its stake. Cheap identities become a losing bet: an ocean of them yields no reliable signal, and one caught lie starts a downward spiral.
